h1: Nakakiri Resort and Spa — a Khwae Noi riverside resort in Thong Pha Phum that's still affordable
intro: Picture waking up, opening your door, and finding mist drifting over the Khwae Noi River with mountains as a backdrop, and a cool, easy air that Kanchanaburi town can't give you — Nakakiri Resort and Spa is a riverside resort in Hin Dat sub-district, Thong Pha Phum, that leans into its natural setting at a price that's still within reach · it ranges from floating raft houses and Superior rooms to pool-view villas and a big one-bedroom villa · what many people love is the large outdoor pool, the quiet atmosphere, and being just about 4 km from Hindad Hot Spring · from about ฿900/night, scoring 7.7/10 and Tripadvisor 3.5/5 from 44 reviews

body.html: Who Nakakiri Resort and Spa is for — to put it as simply as possible, Nakakiri is a "good value" riverside resort for people who want to escape the city to sleep to the sound of the river and breathe mountain air on the Thong Pha Phum side of Kanchanaburi, without paying as much as the better-known luxury resorts along the Khwae · it isn't a heavily designed boutique resort selling polish, and it isn't a luxury tented camp selling maximum privacy · it's a large resort of around 83 rooms set on the Khwae Noi in Hin Dat, with rooms on land, villas, and floating raft houses to choose from · real reviews on Tripadvisor, Trip.com, and Traveloka point in the same direction: the people this suits are families bringing kids to swim, groups of friends who want to rent a raft house for a low-key party by the river, and seminar groups that need a place with a meeting room and plenty of space · on the flip side, couples chasing total romantic quiet, or anyone expecting a brand-new luxury resort, should set their expectations first, because this is a "friendly, good value, nature-forward" resort rather than a premium luxury stay · the real selling points are the riverside location, the mountain setting, the big pool, and how close it is to Hindad Hot Spring, which is the reason people choose to stay around here in the first place

Location and getting there — Nakakiri sits at 99 Moo 1, Hin Dat sub-district, Thong Pha Phum, on the Khwae Noi River, a zone fairly deep into the western part of Kanchanaburi · from Kanchanaburi town it's about a 2–2.5 hour drive along Route 323, which has lovely views but some winding mountain stretches, so if you get carsick easily, bring medicine · what makes this location appealing is that it's only about 4 km from Hindad Hot Spring, a popular natural hot spring that locals here like to soak in · it's also within driving distance of Pha Taem Waterfall, waterfalls inside Thong Pha Phum national park, and the Vajiralongkorn Dam (Khao Laem Dam) · the honest caveat is that the resort is far from convenience stores and restaurants outside the resort, so if you're staying, bring food and supplies with you, or plan to eat mainly at the resort · anyone without their own car will find it hard to reach, because public transport into this zone is limited — driving yourself or hiring a car with a driver is recommended

"It's a bit of a long drive but worth it. Waking up to mist over the river in the morning was beautiful, the pool is huge so the kids could play all day, and then you can just drive over to soak at Hindad Hot Spring, it's really close."

Room types and decor — Nakakiri has several room types covering a range of budgets · starting with the Superior Room, around 32 sqm, a standard room on land with air conditioning, a TV, a fridge, a tea/coffee maker, drinking water, and a balcony — the best-value pick for anyone who just wants a comfortable sleep on a budget · stepping up to the highlight here, the Floating House, around 23 sqm, actually floats on the Khwae Noi: open the door and you're looking at water and mountain views, ideal for anyone who wants the classic Kanchanaburi raft-house experience · and the largest is the 1 Bedroom Villa, up to 100 sqm, with a sofa, bathrobes, and a separate bathtub and shower, good for families or anyone who wants more space · there are also Pool View and River View rooms to choose from as you like · on the decor, to be straight with you, reviews say it's simple and unflashy, and some areas are starting to show their age — many reviewers praise the rooms as clean and roomy, while some say the decor looks ordinary and lacks character · one thing to know is that some of the raft houses and riverside rooms have thin walls, so you can hear the room next door, which is a common limitation of wooden raft-house stays in Thailand

Facilities, pool, and spa — the most talked-about highlight at Nakakiri is the large outdoor swimming pool, which many reviewers praise as wide with pleasantly cool water, great for the whole family · there's a separate water park and kids' pool, giving small children a safe place to play, which is why so many families choose to stay here · there's also a spa and massage rooms to relax after a day out or a day of soaking in the hot spring · on the group side, the resort has a meeting and seminar room for large parties, which is both a strength and something to watch — the strength is that it suits corporate groups and tours, but the caveat is that when seminar groups or tour buses are checked in, the atmosphere gets livelier and noisier than usual, so anyone coming for quiet should check the dates before booking · other facilities include free parking, Wi-Fi (strong in the common areas, but weak in spots inside the rooms according to reviews), bicycle rental, and seasonal riverside activities · overall the facilities are plentiful for the price at the level of a 3-star upcountry resort

Food and bar — the resort's main restaurant is Kiri Restaurant, serving Thai and made-to-order dishes with garden and river views · many reviews praise the breakfast as tasty and good value, and sitting down to a relaxed riverside meal in the morning is something many people enjoy · for other meals, since the resort is far from restaurants outside the area, eating at the resort is the main option — a caveat noted in reviews is that the menu is fairly limited and not very varied, especially if you stay several nights, when the choices may start to feel repetitive · so if you're a picky eater or want backup snacks, it's a good idea to stop and buy supplies from Thong Pha Phum town or a convenience store before heading into the resort · for groups renting a raft house, many like to order set meals to eat on the raft with the riverside atmosphere, which is one of the charms of staying along the Khwae · overall the food at Nakakiri lands at "adequate and good value" rather than being a reason you come specifically to eat, but breakfast is a plus that reviews mention often

Service — service is a point that draws fairly consistent praise in real reviews · many staff are described as friendly, smiling, and helpful, with check-in, recommendations for nearby spots, and looking after large groups · for families with kids, staff often get praise for their attentiveness and for helping out at the pool · that said, to be straightforward, because the resort handles both regular guests and seminar groups at the same time, when it's busy responses can be a little slower and the atmosphere more hectic than usual · but overall most people still see service as a strength that gives it the warm feel of an upcountry resort, rather than being formal and cold

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulled together from Tripadvisor, Trip.com, and Traveloka, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the Khwae Noi riverside location with its beautiful natural setting, the mountain views and morning mist, the large pool the kids have fun in, the tasty good-value breakfast, the friendly staff, being close to Hindad Hot Spring so it's easy to keep sightseeing, and prices that are easy on the wallet compared with other resorts along the Khwae · On the caveat side: the most-mentioned issue is thin walls and poor soundproofing in the raft houses, hearing people walking and the room next door, followed by some buildings and decor starting to show age with a musty smell in some rooms, a limited menu, weak Wi-Fi in the rooms, being far from town and shops, and that during some periods when tour groups or seminar buses are checked in it gets lively and noisy enough to disturb the quiet · most of these gripes can be managed by choosing the right room type, preparing for the distance, and setting expectations to match the price, rather than being problems that make people not want to come back

"The room was clean, the staff were lovely, and the kids wouldn't get out of the pool · the only gripe is the raft house has thin walls and we could hear the room next door at night. Next time I'll try a villa on land instead."

Price and value comparison — the starting price for a standard room is about ฿900/night in normal periods, which is very cheap for a riverside resort with a big pool and a spa · Superior rooms and floating raft houses run roughly ฿1,200–2,000 depending on the season and holidays, while the large one-bedroom villa climbs to around ฿3,000 and up · compared with resorts along the Khwae on the Sai Yok side or luxury resorts that start in the several-thousand-baht range, Nakakiri feels very good value in the budget riverside category, especially once you factor in the big pool, breakfast, and the location near Hindad Hot Spring · if you're planning a trip to the Thong Pha Phum side to soak in the hot spring, play in the waterfalls, and you want a budget riverside base for a family or group of friends, this price gives you back more than the number you pay · but if you expect room quality and decor at the level of a luxury resort, understand that the value here comes from the price and the nature, not from luxury

What to know before you book — a few things make the stay go more smoothly · One, prepare for the distance — the resort is about 2–2.5 hours from Kanchanaburi town along a mountain road, so drive yourself and set off early · Two, if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, avoid the raft houses that sit close together and pick a villa on land or an end room instead, because reviews mention thin walls often · Three, bring food, supplies, and personal medicine, because shops outside the resort are far · Four, if you want peace and quiet, ask the resort beforehand whether there will be a seminar group or tour buses checked in during your stay · Five, plan your sightseeing as a loop — once you've come all this way, allow time to soak at Hindad Hot Spring, visit the waterfalls, and see the Vajiralongkorn Dam to make the trip worth it · Six, pick a free-cancellation option if your plans aren't firm yet, because the weather and the mountain road can change your plans

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Nakakiri Resort and Spa is the best fit for families and groups of friends who want to stay on the Khwae Noi on the Thong Pha Phum side on a budget, with a big pool and a location near Hindad Hot Spring · the natural riverside setting, mountain views, good-value breakfast, and friendly staff make it a good base for a nature trip on the western side of Kanchanaburi · if you're after a brand-new luxury boutique resort, total privacy, or rooms with proper soundproofing, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a tented camp or a luxury resort on the Sai Yok side instead · but for a family trip where you want to swim, soak in the hot spring, and fall asleep to the sound of the river at a price you're comfortable paying — Nakakiri meets that need well and is good value, fitting its standing as a long-running popular choice for the Thong Pha Phum area

honestSummary: Nakakiri Resort and Spa is the best resort for anyone who wants to stay on the Khwae Noi on the Thong Pha Phum side on a budget, with a big pool and a location near Hindad Hot Spring — a standout natural setting, good-value breakfast, and friendly staff · but you have to accept it's a simple-style resort, with some buildings starting to show age, thin-walled raft houses, and a location far from town

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Nakakiri Resort and Spa

faq.q: Where is Nakakiri Resort and Spa · how do you get there?
faq.a: The resort is at 99 Moo 1, Hin Dat sub-district, Thong Pha Phum, Kanchanaburi, on the Khwae Noi River · from Kanchanaburi town it's about a 2–2.5 hour drive along Route 323, which has winding mountain stretches · having your own car is recommended, because public transport into this zone is limited, and it's only about 4 km from Hindad Hot Spring

faq.q: What's the starting price at Nakakiri Resort and Spa · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about ฿900/night for a Superior room on land in normal periods · there are floating raft houses (Floating House), pool-view/river-view rooms, and a 100-sqm one-bedroom villa for families · prices rise over long holidays, so compare several platforms and book ahead

It's a great fit for families bringing kids to swim, groups of friends, and seminar groups who want to stay on the Khwae Noi on the Thong Pha Phum side on a budget · there's a big pool, a kids' pool, and it's close to Hindad Hot Spring · if you're after a luxury boutique resort or total privacy, a luxury tented camp or a luxury resort on the Sai Yok side may suit you better

faq.q: What's the noise and privacy like at Nakakiri?
faq.a: Many reviews agree that the wooden raft houses have thin walls and poor soundproofing, so you hear the room next door and people walking · if you're a light sleeper, it's best to pick a villa on land or an end room, and ask beforehand whether there will be a seminar group or tour buses checked in during your stay, because the atmosphere gets livelier than usual at times

faq.q: Does Nakakiri have a pool, a spa, and breakfast?
faq.a: There's a large outdoor swimming pool with a water park and kids' pool that children love · there's a spa and massage rooms to relax · breakfast is included in the room rate at Kiri Restaurant, which many reviews praise as tasty and good value, while the menu for other meals is fairly limited, so bring some food with you just in case

faq.q: What is there to see around Nakakiri?
faq.a: The highlight is Hindad Hot Spring, only about 4 km away · you can also visit Pha Taem Waterfall, waterfalls inside Thong Pha Phum national park, and see the Vajiralongkorn Dam (Khao Laem Dam) within driving distance · it's well suited to a nature trip on the western side of Kanchanaburi using the resort as a base
